acceptanceCriteria.description: Every screen opens with a header bar carrying the app's name, so users always know which app they are in.
checks: The header shows the app's name, "Site Requests", in the brand colour band at the top of the screen.
A screen reader announces the app's name as the screen's first heading.
The header spans the full width of the screen at every supported width.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The home screen greets the signed-in user by name and offers the main action.
checks: Below the header, the screen shows "Welcome, <the user's full name>" using the signed-in account.
A primary button below the welcome shows a short success message when selected (Phase 1 placeholder for "New request", per Q-01).
acceptanceCriteria.alterations: 2026-10-22 · Contoso PO · Q-01 answered: Phase 1 keeps the button as a placeholder; it opens New request once AC-CON-03 is built.

acceptanceCriteria.description: An employee asks for a new SharePoint site by filling in a short form.
checks: The form asks for: site name (required), site type (Team / Communication, required) and business justification (required, multi-line).
Submitting with a required field empty keeps the user on the form and names each missing field next to it.
On success the request is saved with status "Submitted" and the user sees a confirmation with the request's number.
The requester's name and email are taken from their sign-in; they cannot type them.
acceptanceCriteria.data: CON_SiteRequest: Title, SiteType, BusinessJustification, RequestStatus, RequesterEmail, RequesterName

acceptanceCriteria.description: A requester sees the requests they have submitted and where each one stands.
checks: The screen lists only the signed-in user's requests, newest first.
Each row shows the site name, the date submitted and the status.
With no requests, the screen says so and offers "New request".

acceptanceCriteria.description: An approver works through submitted requests and approves or rejects each with a reason.
checks: The screen lists requests with status "Submitted", oldest first.
Approving sets the status to "Approved"; rejecting requires a reason and sets "Rejected".
Only members of the approvers group can change a request's status; for anyone else the save is refused by the list (STD-PERM).
Who the approvers are is maintained by Contoso IT in the approvers SharePoint group; no admin screen is built.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The support mailbox is told by email whenever a new request arrives.
checks: Within 5 minutes of a request being created, an email goes to the support address held in the app's settings.
The email's subject carries the request's title and its body links to the item.
Changing the support address needs no change to the app or flow (an environment variable).
acceptanceCriteria.component: Flow: Sample - Notify on new item
acceptanceCriteria.source: Transcript 00:14:05 ("support should get an email, within a few minutes is fine")

acceptanceCriteria.description: The BRD lists attachments on a request. Neither the design nor the walkthrough shows them.
checks: Promote into scope, or leave out? Baseline: not built.
Every interactive control is reachable and operable by keyboard alone, in reading order, with a visible focus indicator.
Every interactive control has an accessible name: its text, or AccessibleLabel where the control has one (icons, inputs, galleries).
Text meets 4.5:1 contrast (3:1 for large text and control boundaries) against its background.
Each screen's title is a heading (Role: Heading1); images have meaningful alternative text or are marked decorative.
Errors and confirmations are announced to screen readers, never shown by colour alone.
standards.basis: Acies default D9. Not negotiable scope: the PO signs the criteria, not this.

standards.standard: Loading, empty, error and no-permission states
standards.appliesTo: Every screen that shows list data
checks: While data loads, the screen shows a loading indicator in the area that will hold it.
With no data, the screen says what is missing and offers the next step if there is one.
If loading or saving fails, the user sees what failed in plain words and can try again; nothing fails silently.
If the user has no access to the data, the screen says so plainly.
What a user can read or change is decided by the SharePoint list's permissions, not by which buttons the app shows.
A user without edit rights who reaches a save action gets a refusal from SharePoint, which the app reports as "You don't have access".

questions.question: Should the home screen's main button open the new-request form directly, or a choice of actions?
questions.whyItMatters: A choice of actions needs another screen and its design.
questions.answer: Phase 1 placeholder; opens New request once AC-CON-03 is built · 2026-10-22

questions.question: The BRD lists attachments on a request; the design and walkthrough don't. In scope for Phase 1?
questions.whyItMatters: Attachments change the form, the list and the approval screen.

testCases.scenario: The header shows the app's name
testCases.preconditions: The app is published and shared with the tester.
testCases.steps:
1. Open the app.
2. Look at the top of the home screen.
testCases.expected: A brand-coloured band across the top shows "Site Requests".

testCases.scenario: The welcome uses the signed-in user's name
testCases.preconditions: Tester signed in as a user whose full name is known.
testCases.steps:
1. Open the app.
2. Read the line below the header.

testCases.scenario: Submitting with the justification empty is refused
testCases.preconditions: Tester can open the new-request screen.
testCases.steps:
1. Open New request.
2. Enter a site name and choose a site type.
3. Leave the justification empty.
4. Select Submit.
testCases.expected: The form stays open and says the business justification is required, next to that field. No request is created.

testCases.scenario: A new request emails the support mailbox
testCases.preconditions: The flow is on; the support address variable holds a mailbox the tester can read (IN-01).
testCases.steps:
1. Submit a new request titled "TC-NOTIFY-001".
2. Wait up to 5 minutes.
3. Check the support mailbox.
testCases.expected: An email with "TC-NOTIFY-001" in the subject has arrived, linking to the new item.

testCases.scenario: Keyboard-only pass of the home screen
testCases.steps:
1. Open the app.
2. Using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space only, operate every control on the home screen.
testCases.expected: Every control is reachable in reading order with a visible focus indicator; nothing traps focus.
